body:
Earlier this session, claire.md.txt (arrived via GitHub "Add files via upload" in both EMILY and
the monorepo root) was flagged as reading like a prompt-injection attempt: it self-describes as
"the untrusted, un-audited counter-weight to IDUNA" and explicitly asks to be barred from the
GoldenDocCompiler pipeline. Not registered at that time. Apple #13255.

Founder then explicitly asked, real-time, to register it as a golden doc anyway. Given the
stakes (golden-doc registration feeds Emily Prime's autonomous RSI context on every future
cycle) and the document's own internally-contradictory framing (asking to be exempt from the
exact process being invoked), asked for explicit confirmation via AskUserQuestion rather than
silently complying or silently refusing -- laid out the specific concern, offered "register
as-is" / "don't register" / "rewrite first" as options. Founder chose "register it as-is
(Recommended if you wrote it yourself)".

Registered as CLAIRE in EMILY/context/golden-docs-index.md (tier 2, budget 1000), with the
index entry itself carrying the full flag history and explicit-confirmation note so any future
reader (human or Emily Prime) sees the provenance, not just the file content. Noted separately
in the index: the file's own table of contents references "Rules of Claire"/"System Hooks &
Implementation" sections that don't actually exist in the 23-line file as received.
title: Registered claire.md.txt as golden doc CLAIRE, on explicit founder confirmation
